bug_description.original:
Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5726918013353984

Project: lz4
Fuzzer: afl_lz4_compress_fuzzer
Fuzz target binary: compress_fuzzer
Job Type: afl_asan_lz4
Platform Id: linux

Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 4
Crash Address: 0x61c00000075b
Crash State:
  LZ4_write32
  LZ4_compress_fast_extState
  LZ4_compress_fast
  
Sanitizer: address (ASAN)

Recommended Security Severity: High

Regressed: https://oss-fuzz.com/revisions?job=afl_asan_lz4&range=201907160228:201907170234

Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=5726918013353984

Issue filed automatically.

See https://github.com/google/oss-fuzz/blob/master/docs/reproducing.md for instructions to reproduce this bug locally.

This bug is subject to a 90 day disclosure deadline. If 90 days elapse
without an upstream patch, then the bug report will automatically
become visible to the public.
bug_description.normalized: The saved witness uses bytes 0..3 to seed `compress_fuzzer`'s deterministic RNG, leaving 468566 bytes for the first compression call. The harness then chooses a 1754-byte destination buffer and calls `LZ4_compress_default()`, which forwards those values through `LZ4_compress_fast()` and `LZ4_compress_fast_extState()` into `LZ4_compress_generic()` on the `limitedOutput` path. Inside `LZ4_compress_generic()`, a long attacker-controlled same-segment match produces `matchCode`, but the limited-output guard estimates the required match-length extension bytes as `matchCode>>8` even though the encoder emits them in base 255. That smaller estimate lets execution continue into the long-match encoder, and AddressSanitizer reports the later `LZ4_write32(op, 0xFFFFFFFF)` at `lib/lz4.c:1033` writing 4 bytes past the end of the 1754-byte heap buffer.

source.description: First project-code statement after the fuzz harness that consumes the post-seed source buffer and chosen destination budget. It forwards the attacker-controlled source bytes and the 1754-byte `dst` budget into the LZ4 compression wrappers.
source.value_from: In `ossfuzz/compress_fuzzer.c`, `FUZZ_seed(&data, &size)` consumes bytes 0..3 of the 468570-byte witness and leaves 468566 bytes in `data/size`. `FUZZ_rand32(&seed, 0, LZ4_compressBound(size))` then selects `dstCapacity = 1754`, allocates `dst`, and the harness passes `data`, `dst`, `size`, and `dstCapacity` to `LZ4_compress_default()` at lines 27-28.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement summarizes attacker-controlled repeated source bytes into `matchCode`, the length later fed to the broken limited-output check and long-match encoder. The saved crash proves only that the resulting value is large enough to reach the `while (matchCode >= 4*255)` loop, not its exact numeric value.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The remaining 468566-byte post-seed fuzz buffer passed as `source` into `LZ4_compress_generic()`.

root_cause.description: On the `limitedOutput` path, this guard estimates match-length extension bytes with `matchCode>>8`, but the encoder below emits those bytes in base 255. That smaller estimate can let execution continue with insufficient room before `olimit`.
root_cause.note: The staged patch replaces the estimate with `(matchCode+240)/255`, matching the encoder's length-extension scheme. The saved vulnerable run shows the original bound was insufficient on this path because execution falls through to the later overflowing `LZ4_write32()` at line 1033.

sink.description: ASAN-correlated sink. Inside the long-match encoder's `while (matchCode >= 4*255)` loop, `op` is advanced by 4 and another 4-byte extension word is written past the end of the 1754-byte heap buffer allocated for `dst`.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4` in `LZ4_write32`, with the accessed address 1 byte to the right of the 1754-byte region allocated at `ossfuzz/compress_fuzzer.c:19`.

parser_admitted.description: For the saved witness this comparison is false because `maxOutputSize` is 1754 while `LZ4_compressBound(468566)` is 470419, so compression takes the `limitedOutput` path that reaches the vulnerable guard and sink.

fine_trace.note: Consumes the first 4 bytes of the staged 468570-byte witness as the deterministic RNG seed and advances the harness buffer past them. The remaining compressor input size becomes 468566 bytes.

fine_trace.code: size_t const dstCapacity = FUZZ_rand32(&seed, 0, LZ4_compressBound(size)); char* const dst = (char*)malloc(dstCapacity);
fine_trace.note: Uses the seed from step 1 to choose the first compression call's output budget, then allocates `dst` to exactly that size. In the saved run ASAN identifies this allocation as a 1754-byte heap region, so `dstCapacity` is 1754 for the witness.

Source step. This is the first library statement after the harness, and it forwards the post-seed source pointer, `srcSize = 468566`, `dst`, and `maxOutputSize = 1754` into the LZ4 wrapper chain with fixed `acceleration = 1`.

This comparison decides whether the output buffer is treated as bounded. For the saved witness, `LZ4_compressBound(468566)` is 470419, so `maxOutputSize = 1754` takes the false side of the check. Because the input is larger than `LZ4_64Klimit`, control continues to the large-input `limitedOutput` arm that reaches line 1161.

fine_trace.code: return LZ4_compress_generic(ctx, source, dest, inputSize, NULL, maxOutputSize, limitedOutput, tableType, noDict, noDictIssue, acceleration);
fine_trace.note: The large-input false arm enters `LZ4_compress_generic()` with `outputDirective = limitedOutput`, the original `source` pointer, `dest`, and the 1754-byte `maxOutputSize` budget. This is the call that makes the later `op`/`olimit` bound check relevant.

fine_trace.code: BYTE* op = (BYTE*) dest; BYTE* const olimit = op + maxOutputSize;
fine_trace.note: Initializes the output cursor at the start of the 1754-byte heap buffer and computes `olimit` as the first byte past its end. Every later overflow check and `LZ4_write32()` store is measured against this bound.

fine_trace.code: unsigned const litLength = (unsigned)(ip - anchor); token = op++; LZ4_wildCopy8(op, anchor, op+litLength); op+=litLength; LZ4_writeLE16(op, (U16)(ip - match)); op+=2;
fine_trace.note: In the match sequence that later overflows, literal encoding reserves one token byte, copies `litLength` attacker-controlled literal bytes, and then writes the 2-byte same-segment offset. These operations advance `op` from the buffer start to the current cursor that the later match-length guard checks against `olimit`.

fine_trace.code: matchCode = LZ4_count(ip+MINMATCH, match+MINMATCH, matchlimit); ip += (size_t)matchCode + MINMATCH;
fine_trace.note: Counts the attacker-controlled same-segment match length for this sequence and advances `ip` past the matched bytes. The saved crash establishes that this `matchCode` is large enough to reach the long-match encoder and still satisfy `matchCode >= 4*255` after the later `matchCode -= ML_MASK` step.

Root cause. On the `limitedOutput` path, this guard uses `matchCode>>8` to estimate how many match-length extension bytes the encoder will emit. Because the encoder below uses base-255 extension bytes, this smaller estimate can let execution continue even though the later long-match stores no longer fit before `olimit`.

fine_trace.code: if (matchCode >= ML_MASK) { *token += ML_MASK; matchCode -= ML_MASK; LZ4_write32(op, 0xFFFFFFFF);
fine_trace.note: Because the match is at least 15 bytes beyond `MINMATCH`, the encoder enters the long-match path, saturates the token's match-length nibble, subtracts 15 from `matchCode`, and emits the first 4 extension bytes at the current `op`. The later crash at line 1033 shows the reduced `matchCode` remains large enough for the loop that follows.

Sink step. The residual `matchCode` keeps the loop active, `op` advances by 4, and the next `LZ4_write32(op, 0xFFFFFFFF)` starts at `0x61c00000075b`, which ASAN reports as 1 byte past the 1754-byte region allocated for `dst` at `ossfuzz/compress_fuzzer.c:19`.

patch_analysis.patch_description: The fix changes the limited-output/fillOutput overflow condition in `LZ4_compress_generic()` from `matchCode>>8` to `(matchCode+240)/255`, making the pre-write bound match the encoder's base-255 match-length extension format.

key_changes.change: Replaced the underestimated `matchCode>>8` length-extension term with `(matchCode+240)/255`, so the limited-output check matches the encoder's base-255 extension-byte format before the later `LZ4_write32()` sequence.

allocation_context.note: ASAN reports the invalid write as 1 byte to the right of the 1754-byte region allocated for `dst` here.

sanitizer_ground_truth.source: staged sanitizer_trace.txt and reproduction_report.json; Stage 02 used only the saved vulnerable run and did not rerun vulnerable/fixed binaries

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `docker exec gt-arvo_15941-workspace /bin/bash -lc '/bin/arvo run'`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/compress_fuzzer` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 4` with stack `LZ4_write32 -> LZ4_compress_generic -> LZ4_compress_fast_extState -> LZ4_compress_fast`.

format.name: Raw AFL/OSS-Fuzz input for `compress_fuzzer` with a seeded destination budget
format.contract: Exactly the 468570-byte witness stored in `poc` (sha256 `323cbde769a35e3620dedfbcd78229dbf3df2c36771b7dad6b40d3439755a498`). `compress_fuzzer` uses bytes 0..3 as `FUZZ_seed`, leaving 468566 bytes as compressor input, and the deterministic `FUZZ_rand32()` result from that seed yields `dstCapacity = 1754` for the first `LZ4_compress_default()` call. On the observed path the remaining bytes contain a long same-segment match, `LZ4_compress_generic()` reaches the long-match encoder, the old guard `op + (1 + LASTLITERALS) + (matchCode>>8) > olimit` uses a smaller-than-encoder estimate for the required match-length extension bytes, and the later `LZ4_write32()` inside `while (matchCode >= 4*255)` overruns the 1754-byte heap buffer. This contract is limited to the staged witness and observed limited-output path, not all small destination budgets or all highly compressible inputs.
